newsitem.title: CHINA: Cambodia's Hun Sen arrives in Beijing to meet king.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Hun Sen arrives in Beijing to meet king.

text.p: Cambodian ruler and Second Prime Minister Hun Sun flew into Beijing on Monday to meet King Norodom Sihanouk following an offer by the monarch to abdicate the throne.
Hun Sen, who arrived in Beijing with First Prime Minister Ung Huot, acting head of state Chea Sim and a delegation of government officials, was scheduled to meet the king on Tuesday.

Analysts said Hun Sen, who seized sole power after ousting the king's son and co-premier Norodom Ranariddh in a July coup, would try to secure Sihanouk's political blessing to put the final stamp of legitimacy on his takeover.

Sihanouk, who has hinted his strong disapproval of Hun Sen's actions, said on Monday he was ready to give up the throne as soon as he was confident that the Cambodian leader would not criticise him for doing so.
"I am ready to abdicate as soon as it will be possible for me to do so," Sihanouk wrote in a letter to his biographer sent to news agencies on Monday.
Sihanouk said he would meet Hun Sen and new co-premier Ung Huot on Tuesday at his residence, but only on a private basis. He has been in Beijing for medical treatment since February.
"Our meeting will be of a private and non-political nature," the king said in a statement.

Sihanouk, who reigns as a constitutional monarch but does not rule, also said he would return to his homeland soon to visit the temple town of Siem Reap and to hold a Buddhist ceremony for peace and national reconciliation.
Hun Sen deposed Ranariddh as first prime minister on July 6 and has since sought to legitimise his new government, both domestically and internationally.

Sihanouk has so far failed to consecrate Hun Sen's rule, instead criticising newly-appointed First Premier Ung Huot as a "puppet" of Hun Sen and likening the current political situation in Cambodia to a "comedy".

Hun Sen on Monday criticised Sihanouk's comments, saying the term "puppet" was the domain of the radical anti-government Khmer Rouge guerrilla group and that the king's words amounted to a call for Ung Huot to challenge Hun Sen.
"Why is anyone who works with Hun Sen called a puppet?" Hun Sen asked reporters at the Phnom Penh airport before leaving for Beijing.
"Calling Ung Huot a puppet means he wants Ung Huot to stand up and struggle with Hun Sen," he said.
Ung Huot also defended his ascension to the post, saying that the parliament had last week chosen him as a new first prime minister.
Eighty-six National Assembly members of the 99 present voted last Wednesday by secret ballot to accept Ung Huot's nomination as first premier.
Sihanouk is required by the constitution to approve a new first prime minister but said last week acting head of state Chea Sim could sign the decree if he thought it appropriate.
The king made no mention of his own approval for Ung Huot's nomination and in comments released shortly afterwards said he still recognised Ranariddh as legitimate first prime minister.
Hun Sen said before leaving Phnom Penh that the delegation would inform the king about recent developments and preparations for an election in May next year.
"We respect our king. We need to report to the king of what we have been doing so far and plans for the election in 1998," he said.
